items.title: 30.5 Predicting the 1H NMR Spectrum of a Given Molecule

source_refs.note: Topic 30.5 with Example 30.1 and Quick Check 30.5, answered (PDF 210). Answers need review.

blocks.text: Using chemical environments, chemical shifts and splitting, the 1H NMR spectrum of a given molecule can be predicted from its structure.

items: Identify the different proton environments: the number of environments is the number of peaks expected.
Estimate the chemical shift of each set of equivalent protons from Table 30.1; protons near electronegative atoms have higher shifts, those in alkyl groups lower ones.
Predict the splitting pattern of each peak with the n + 1 rule.
Assign the relative peak areas from the number of hydrogen atoms in each environment.

blocks.title: Example 30.1: chloroethane, CH3CH2Cl
blocks.text: Two environments, so two peaks. The CH2 is attached to electronegative Cl, so it has the higher shift (3.0-4.5 ppm); the CH3 is lower (0.5-1.5 ppm). The CH3 is split by the 2 H of CH2 into a triplet; the CH2 is split by the 3 H of CH3 into a quartet. The peak areas of CH3 and CH2 are 3:2.
For propan-2-ol, (CH3)2CHOH, predict (a) the number of peaks, (b) the type of proton and chemical shift, (c) the relative peak areas, (d) the splitting pattern.
